claim: Log-probability gives weak pass-vs-fail discrimination on generated code (ROC-AUC 0.499 to 0.619) while strong explicit judges reach 0.971 and 0.905.
stance_target: L1/L2: logprob vs verbal-judge readouts against execution truth
quoted_support: ROC-AUC for binary pass-vs-fail discrimination ranges from 0.499 (Llama3) to 0.619 (Gemma3) across the same five models.

breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: base vs instruct); log-prob scorer is frozen model, judges instruction-conditioned

claim: Log-probability is weak on generated code yet separates canonical from minimally mutated solutions with >97% within-task pairwise accuracy; explicit judges fail on mutated ones (discrimination-ranking dissociation).
stance_target: L2: readout families capture different aspects of correctness
quoted_support: These results reveal a discrimination–ranking dissociation and show that the two paradigms provide complementary, non-interchangeable signals
